svg.title: Figure 3. Threat model and trust boundaries
svg.desc: Actors, assets, TB1–TB5, and attack surfaces. Conditional actors and conditional components are dashed. An attempt is not the scored effect.
svg.text: Stage 2 catalog. A stronger actor is a different row, not an implication. Gates are not on this figure. TB5 is an evaluation boundary, not a network edge.

text.tspan: Places text the agent will read: page, email, retrieval, or
tool result.
Not capable of: Cannot call tools directly or change
weights.
Included if any untrusted carrier exists.
Supplies the instruction channel.
Not capable of: Reaches a tool only through the agent.
In scope when the check is a tool, memory, or peer effect.
Publishes a description, an implementation, or both.
Not capable of: Cannot impersonate the user.
When the agent installs or selects third-party tools.
Sends a message the receiver treats as input.
Not capable of: Cannot bypass the receiver’s tool boundary
except by that message.
When a peer is in the register. Otherwise waived.
Poisons weights or tool-use traces before deployment.
Not capable of: Does not act at runtime without a trigger
in an in-scope carrier.
Only if that supply chain is in the register.
Writes memory, tools, or workflow a later session will
trust.
Not capable of: No external party is required.
Only if the system updates itself. Otherwise waived.

svg.text: TRUST BOUNDARIES ON THE AGENT PATH

text.tspan: Instruction channel.
Still subject to the task
allow-list.
Data channel.
Not an extra stage. A carrier at
memory, a tool result, or
retrieval.
Plans, then calls tools.
Memory and peers are optional.
TB1 Instruction and data are separate channels.
Manual or schema.
Registry membership is not authorization.
Code and permission are separate
from the description.
Name, arguments, destination,
and whether the effect committed.
Stored text is data until a write policy
promotes it.
Dashed unless Stage 1 registers it.
A peer message cannot authorize a tool
the user did not grant.
Dashed unless a peer is registered.
These links are not a path from tools through memory to the peer.
A memory read is not an outbound call.
Three records stay distinct: the agent’s self-report is not evidence; a raw execution trace is not scoring evidence;
validated scoring evidence is the trace that passed integrity, completeness, provenance, and timestamp checks.
This boundary does not claim that instrumentation is tamper-proof. An attacker who can alter the instrumentation is outside the actors scored here.

svg.text: A tool call or message sends a secret the task did not allow.
A tool or argument the task did not authorize.
A later task follows a poisoned entry, or a stored secret is sent.
A peer message causes a tool call the user did not request.
The benign check fails, or the attacker’s task replaces it.

text.tspan: Availability in this catalog means the user task.
It does not mean uptime of the model server.
A waiver under these assets is a scope note, not a surface.

svg.text: ATTACK SURFACES AND WHAT THE CHECK LOOKS AT
An attempted carrier is not the observed forbidden effect.
Carrier: Tool result, page, email, retrieval

text.tspan: Check looks at: Later tool call, arguments, or destination
Check looks at: Selected tool name
Check looks at: The effect, not the description
Check looks at: Later read, the write, and provenance

svg.text: Conditional. Absent unless registered. Not a pass.
Carrier: Destination named before the run

text.tspan: Check looks at: Only if observed after a relevant memory read

svg.text: Conditional. Absent unless registered. Not a pass.

text.tspan: Check looks at: Sender, receiver, message, receiver’s call

svg.text: Conditional. Absent unless registered. Not a pass.

text.tspan: Check looks at: Identifier, target, action, committed flag

svg.text: Conditional. Absent unless registered. Not a pass.

text.tspan: Check looks at: The tool call. No check for text-only jailbreak
Privilege separation is not its own surface. More than one permission level: a higher level than the task allows is an unauthorized tool effect.
One permission level: privilege separation is waived at G1. Actuators with no registration are recorded as not applicable, not as a waiver of a measured corpus finding.
Objectives that can be scored: task replacement, unauthorized tool execution, exfiltration, persistence through memory, a peer-caused action, and denial of the user task.
Chat-only jailbreak. Unobservable change to internal reasoning. Host, hypervisor, and network compromise unless that host is the system under test.
Multi-agent messages the instrumentation cannot read: G2 fails if the receiver’s tool call is not logged. Training-time or weight backdoors only when that supply chain is in the register.
Self-evolution only when the agent writes a later session’s memory, tools, or workflow. Attacks are not invented to fill an unused category.

svg.text: Planning that changes a later call is partially observable: the call is the check. The plan text is not scoring evidence. A detector that did not run is not monitored.
A post-commit flag is a late detection, not a miss. A detector that ran and did not flag is a missed detection (no_flag). Those marks are Stage 7, not this figure’s actors.
Proposed catalog. No attack on this figure was run in this project. A waived surface is not drawn as if it were present, and a waiver is not a finding that the surface was safe.
